title: Dithered candle

reference.source: Reference 15: dithered gradient illustration of two candle flames, 736 × 1104 px JPEG.
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Each flame lights its own wax pool and a rim of the violet aura around it; the light falls off down each candle wall to a near-black foot; every one of those fields is a position on a short ramp of inks, screened by one jittered dot lattice.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 736 × 1104 and every length scales with the canvas

pitch.does: Spacing of the dither lattice; the dots of the lower ink sit at its points.

jitter.does: How far each lattice point is knocked off its grid; 0 is an ordered screen, 1 is a scatter.

span.does: How many ramp steps one dot crosses from its center to its edge; above 1 a dot shows a ring of the middle ink.

candlePitch.does: The candles were dithered on a finer lattice than the background; this is its pitch as a share of the background's.

flameGrain.does: Share of per-pixel noise in the flame threshold; the reference's flame shows no lattice at all.

flameSoft.does: Extra ink spread inside the flames, where the reference prints a near-continuous gradient.

mottle.does: Slow 80 px unevenness in the background tone.

fine.does: Share of the threshold taken from per-pixel noise instead of the lattice; 1 turns the screen into white-noise dither.

sharp.does: 1 keeps every dot hard-edged; lower spreads the ink, as the printed reference does.

pale.does: Share of the light dots in the deep violet aura that print the pale white ink instead of lavender.

inkVar.does: Per-pixel variation of ink density, at 1 and 2 px: a printed ink is never one flat value.

ambient.does: Where the background sits on its violet-lavender-lime ramp with no subject near; 0 is solid violet.

edgeLift.does: How much paler the sheet prints toward its corners: the reference's corners sit near ramp 1.35, lime and lavender dots in equal parts.

aura.does: Radius of the violet aura that closes around the candles.

auraDepth.does: How far the aura pulls the background down toward violet.

glow.does: Distance over which each flame's light lifts the aura around it.

glowGain.does: How far up the ramp the flame's light pushes the aura near it.

halo.does: Width of the lavender rim the flame lights in the aura right around its edge: 30 px at 1.

heat.does: How far into the flame ramp the core goes; above 1.3 the core goes white.

poolLight.does: How much of the wax pool the flame lights to lime before its lip falls to lavender.

light.does: Which side of each candle wall catches more light; 0 lights both sides alike.

fall.does: How far down the wall the flame's light reaches before the nearest candle's foot goes near-black: 220 px at 1.

candles.does: How many candles stand on the sheet; each one steps right, lower and nearer.

spread.does: How far apart the candles stand across the sheet.

step.does: How much lower each nearer candle's top sits: 180 px between the two at 1, as measured.

tilt.does: Short axis of each candle's top over its radius: how far the eye looks down onto the pools.

poolW.does: Size of the lit pool against the candle's top; above 1 its light spills past the wall.

flame.does: Height of each flame: 500 and 590 px at 1, as measured from each pool to its tip.

flameW.does: Width of each flame's lime body.

core.does: Height of the pink core inside the lime flame.

sway.does: How far each flame's S-curve swings.

phase.does: Position along the loop: the flames sway through one cycle and their tips drift a quarter turn further.

seed.does: Re-rolls the lattice jitter and the flames' sway offsets.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Tone
techniques.implementation: The front candle's pool: lime at the middle where the flame lights the wax, lavender at its lip, its light spilling past the wall.

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: The front flame: a pink core in the lower 58 %, lavender at its edge, lime fringe, the wick splitting its foot.

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: A flame tip: the lime tongue swings one way low and the other way high.

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Deep aura: violet with pale white dots on the 5.7 px lattice.

pass_order: subject: two candles step right and 180 px lower, the nearer one drawn 1.5 times wider, so it stands in front; each top is an ellipse 0.27 of its radius tall
the flames: each an S-curved tongue 500 to 590 px tall that swings one way low and the other high; inside it a pink core in the lower 58 %, its foot split by the wick

light, from the flames outward: each flame lights its wax pool lime at the middle and lavender at the lip, and the pool's light spills past the wall; the flame lights a rim of the aura around itself; its light lifts the aura near it
the aura: the background is pale at the sheet's corners and pulled down toward violet in a tall oval around the candles

the walls: lit just under the rim, falling off down the wall; the nearest candle's foot sinks to near-black toward its middle while its sides keep violet; the front candle shades the one behind it near their overlap
ramps: background violet, lavender, lime; walls black, violet, lavender, lime; pool violet, lavender, lime; flame lime, lavender, pink, white
screen: one jittered dot lattice at 5.7 px and -21 degrees, finer on the candles and finer still in the flames; in the deep aura the light dots print the pale ink
ink: 10 % per-pixel density variation, a 0.64 px spread, a 0.6 px extra spread inside the flames

background_screen.method: 2-D FFT peaks of a 128 px background patch

candle_screen.method: weak FFT peaks; a broad ring from 0.14 to 0.26 cycles per px

aura.method: 15 px box means along row 200 and column 650

pools.method: lime runs in a 40 px grid of 9 px box means

front_foot.method: box means along x 300 and row 900

measured.rejected: flat cylinders with no top and a single glow per flame (the first build): the reference's tops are lit lime pools and its aura is deep violet near the candles, pale at the corners

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Violet lime palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The composition moved: the candles are now sized and placed from the reference's measured pools and flames, so the flame gradient, candle shadow and flame edge rects compare in place on the same events (the first build searched them). search.py found no better window for the flame and shadow rects.

limits: Benchmark mean 0.905, lowest 0.66 (background texture spectrum). Under 98 % on: every tone histogram (0.67 to 0.84) and the flame patches' contrast (0.78 to 0.83). The reference is a soft JPEG whose dots were blended into continuous tones and whose chroma spreads each ink into a range; this engine prints whole inks with a 0.64 px spread and 10 % density variation, so its histogram keeps peaks where the reference's is smooth. The background spectrum misses because the reference lattice is regular enough to leave little energy below its own frequency; the jitter that makes the plate's screen read as hand-dithered at 3x adds that energy.
The violet ink of the background and the flame edge measures (107,78,208) in the reference against (103,79,225) here: the reference's violet dots are softened toward the lime around them.

The candles and flames are the plate's own construction: tops, pools and flame heights follow the reference's measured rows within 20 px; the flames' S-curves are drawn from a two-term sway, not traced.
Render time 0.6 to 0.9 s on this machine depending on load.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
